title: Sampled average block time can start after the block that must be scanned
prompt: A reviewer is checking a block-timestamp start estimator for a log backfill. The chain is synthetic and its block time is monotonic. The estimator under review reads the head, takes one sample block from a guess based on the nominal block time, divides the elapsed time by the block span to get an average block time, and uses that average to pick a start block. Compute the sample block, its timestamp, the start block the estimator returns, and the first block whose timestamp is at or after the target. Then say whether the step block is still inside the range the backfill would scan going forward from the returned start. This is one constructed counterexample to the sampling estimator, not a correct production algorithm.

estimator_under_review.sample: read block at guess; sampleTimestamp = T(guess)
estimator_under_review.averageNs: floor(elapsed * 1e9 / span), integer division as in a Go duration
estimator_under_review.returnedStart: max(head - ceil(ago * 1e9 / averageNs), 0), then scan forward only

provenance: Constructed by BlockVectra for this dataset. Motivation and the reviewed algorithm: https://github.com/Munyon-Canyon/monaco/blob/f92222599f2945c0662e9263d57756f658015f59/apps/backend/internal/modules/trading/adapters/evm_arrivals.go#L284-L302 and https://github.com/Munyon-Canyon/monaco/pull/5462#issuecomment-6359666637. No third-party code, issue text, or private data is copied, and the links do not claim upstream adopted this case or that it was reproduced on a real chain.
scope: One synthetic counterexample to a sampled-average start estimator. Not a correct production algorithm, not a fix, and not a real chain trace.
